about: What a host-served <send> and a host-run <invoke> hand the host, written out by hand (docs/adr/0084, D4 and D6).
Each case names a document beside this table and one element of it, and gives the request
core/HostProcessor.h defines as the host receives it: a HostSendRequest for a send, a
HostInvokeRequest for an invoke. An invoke's `token` and `sessionId` are left out, since
they are the engine's own and differ between engines by design; `restarted` is false for
every case. `params` are what the handler is handed: a deadline the engine keeps
(`_sce_deadline_ms`) is taken out, while `eventData` is the pairs as a local delivery
of a send with them would carry them, the deadline among them. `content` is the text of an
inline <content> without the whitespace that lays it out.
Read by the Interpreter (tests/integration/HostRequestTest.cpp), which runs every
document, and by the generated C++ engine (tests/integration/HostRequestAotTest.cpp),
which runs statechart_host_request.scxml. A case with `lowered` is a Mesh request, which
the generated C++ engine routes through its own router; for it the build's lowering
(host_processor_analyzer::lower_mesh, SCE_MESH.md section 19) is held to the case
instead: the invoke's `src` and `srcexpr` after the lowering, its params in order, and
which of them are envelope fields, whose literal values are the request's.

cases.name: a send to a host processor
an invoke with an evaluated src, a namelist and a repeated param
an invoke with inline content laid out over lines
an invoke with a deadline the engine keeps
a Mesh request to a peer named at run time
a Mesh request to a literal peer, its deadline spelled with the alias
